newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura asset management firms to merge in Oct 1997.
newsitem.headline: Nomura asset management firms to merge in Oct 1997.

text.p: Two Nomura group asset management companies said on Wednesday that they have agreed to merge on October 1, 1997.
The two firms are Nomura Investment Management Co Ltd and Nomura Securities Investment Trust Management Co Ltd.
The merged company will seek to become a top-class asset management company, the two companies said in a statement.
Nomura Investment Management manages assets worth about 3.62 trillion yen and Nomura Securities Investment Trust manages assets worth about 11.79 trillion yen, the statement said.
Nomura Investment Management manages small-lot funds from individual investors and Nomura Securities Investment Trust Management manages corporate pension funds and other large funds.

Nomura Investment Management posted revenues of 3.90 billion yen and Nomura Securities Investment Trust Management posted revenues of 63.64 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1996, the statement said.
"The new company's management policy is to seriously consider customers' profits," the statement said.
The two companies will form a committee to discuss specific details regarding the planned merger, they said.

Toru Tsuchida, President of Nomura Securities Investment Trust Management, told a news conference that the two firms agreed to merge in order to boost asset management capabilities, as well as the research and development of new financial products.

"We would like to form an internationally competitive system because regulations on asset management are being lifted (in Japan)," Tadashi Takubo, president of Nomura Investment Management, said at the same news conference.

People are watching how Japanese individual financial assets worth 1,200 trillion yen will be invested towards the year 2001 when the Japanese version of "Big Bang" financial reform will be completed, Takubo said.
The two presidents said that the companies will not cut jobs because of the merger.

Tsuchida said in order to improve the quality of asset management and research, it is likely that the merged company will increase its workforce. Currently, the combined number of employees at the two firms, excluding foreign employees at their overseas units, total 550 people.
The two presidents also said that in order to strengthen their global asset management system, overseas units of the two firms will be merged at the time their parent companies will merge.

Both of them have their respective subsidiaries in New York, London, Luxembourg and Singapore. Besides them, Nomura Investment Management has a unit in Sydney and Nomura Securities Investment Trust Management has a unit in Hong Kong.

Tsuchida said that as an asset management company, he would not oppose over-the-counter sales of investment trusts at bank branches if investment trust management companies are allowed to take measures to improve investment trust products.
